sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Rudiobus is a Continental Celtic god. He is an obscure Gaulish horse-god known from fine bronze figurines of the first century BC. One piece is a prancing horse inscribed sacred to the god Rudiobus. The bronzes were found at Neuvy-en-Sullias in the valley of the Loire. The statue may show the god in horse form, or it may be an offering made to him. Rather than a native god, Rudiobus may be one aspect of the Gaulish Mars. That god is also called Mullo, a name that may mean mule.

okr.objective: Present Rudiobus as a Gaulish horse-god of the Loire valley.
